# nova-tools roadmap

<!-- Generated from docs/roadmap.sexp by tools/roadmap. Do not edit this file: edit docs/roadmap.sexp and run `make roadmap`. -->

This is the work after the point releases. The release plan (the owner, 2026-10-11) replaces the ladder of 2026-10-09. The v1.2.x point releases come first and are cut in turn: v1.2.10 (being cut), v1.2.11 small fixes, v1.2.12 tests and models only, v1.2.13 contraction (fewer lines, no behaviour change), v1.2.14 the next small fixes; FIXES.md holds each one's scope and fixes, and an item below whose target is a v1.2.x release is waiting for its card. The aim is v1.2.x working pretty well, so it is the reference for intended behaviour: v1.3, unstable, is the re-architecture (the client/server conversion, then each layer secured from the bottom), built by the sprint running on v1.2.x and checked against it, rather than a blind rewrite; like getting a compiler self-hosting, then using it to build a better compiler. v1.4 is the stable release of v1.3, architecturally correct top to bottom. Every item's :release is one of four values (the owner, 2026-10-12): v1.2.x (a point release, named in the item's text), v1.3, v1.4 (stabilization: tests, models and cleanups, no features) or later (a list, not a release); the roadmap tool refuses any other. The v1.3 work is grouped by theme below, in build order, behind the v1.3 test plan that every v1.3 entry lands after; each v1.3 item ends with the behaviour that proves it done (Done when), measurable on the bench, and names the items it absorbed in the de-duplication of 2026-10-12. Point releases continue until only architectural items are open: an area stops taking point fixes when a fix there is the same problem in another form, or would be its third, and each v1.3 architectural item names the point fixes it replaces. Friend work is dogfooded within the week, once more friends are online: friends alone, then friends and fleet together, each friend bug a point-release card. nova-sprint, nova-card and nova-work moved to mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint with the split (v1.2.3), and their items are in that repository's ROADMAP.md. Point-release work is in FIXES.md, not here. Each item says what it is and why it waits. Where the code already has part of an item, the item says what exists and covers only the gap.

## Done

Decided and in place. Recorded so the items that measure them have their starting point.

- **Tier defaults on direct providers** (2026-10-09). flash is Mercury 2.5, pro is DeepSeek 4.1 Flash and heavy is DeepSeek v4 Pro, each called on its own provider's API. Mercury 3 becomes heavy when v1.3's global per-model rate limit lands. Direct providers come first; OpenRouter and OpenCode are spillover only. Clean results start at 2026-10-09 22:01Z.
- **nova-sprint split out of nova-tools** (2026-10-10). nova-sprint, nova-card and nova-work, with their models and docs, live in mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint from v1.2.3; CI here refuses their paths.
- **nova-bus wait has no stale git lock or lane file to recover** (2026-10-10). Closed as obsolete, not fixed: issue #2627 was measured on the git message bus, whose checkout held an index.lock and a dirty from-<name> lane file. That bus was removed on 2026-10-04 and nova-bus is Redis only (docs/SPEC-BUS.md), so wait never runs git and has no checkout to leave locked. A recovery for a friend's old message-bus checkout belongs to the consumer that ticks it, not here.

## v1.3: the test plan comes first

The plan every v1.3 entry lands behind: the test tiers, the bench hosts per tier and the pass bar. Nothing in v1.3 lands before it (the owner, 2026-10-12).

### The v1.3 test plan

Written before any v1.3 code, as docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md in this repository (drafted apart from this entry; this entry tracks it). The tiers every theme ships with: unit (twin or fake store, parallel, under a minute); functional (real Redis and Postgres, one test per Lua function); integration (seat, member and friend together on a bench); stress and load (the measured drags: deals of 3,000 cards, a 140-width fleet, 200 reads, the bus at 10 messages a second); TLA+ (a model with reversed witnesses, TLC on a bench); release checks (the parallel functional suite under two minutes). Bench hosts per tier: the Linux benches hetzner2, space and vision run the functional, integration, stress and TLC tiers; the darwin pool runs the darwin-only functional packages; the studio never runs a tier. The pass bar: green before and after each change, the measured numbers recorded with the run. No v1.3 card lands without its tier's tests; every v1.3 entry in this roadmap and in nova-sprint's lands only after this one, and each theme's own test-plan entry refines it. Done when: docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md is committed naming every tier, bench host and load number above, and nova-sprint add refuses a v1.3 card whose brief names no tier of it.

Why it waits: The owner, 2026-10-12: the plan is created before a line of v1.3 code is written.

Target: v1.3

From: the owner, 2026-10-12

## v1.3 A. Comms foundation

The server is Redis on tailscale; one shared comms module (Lua in Redis and Go) holds presence, capability and timers; nova-hook is the one way in; nova-bus stays the one mail path. Entries are in build order, the theme's test plan first.

### Comms foundation: test plan

The comms theme's tests, written from docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md before the theme's first implementation entry, which cites this one: unit tests on the twin or fake store; functional tests on a real Redis, one per Lua function of pkg/comms; an integration run of seat, member and friend hooked to one server on the bench; the stress drags the theme touches (the bus at 10 messages a second; presence and timers for 140 clients); tla/Comms.tla with its reversed witnesses, checked by TLC on a bench; and its rows in the parallel release checks, under two minutes. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: each tier above has a named test or TLC case for the comms theme, listed in docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md, red before the theme's code and green after, with the 10 messages a second and 140-client presence numbers recorded.

Target: v1.3

From: the owner, 2026-10-12

### The comms link, presence and timers are modelled

tla/Comms.tla, the model the three entries after it cite: a client connects to the server (Redis on tailscale) and the server pushes to it. Truth outside the store per client (a live tool turn is the one state that consumes a fire); the store holds a fresh incarnation (never a counter), presence by session generation and sequence, the link as last evidence with two deadlines (the hard process deadline, immutable, and the renewable proof, never past hard), listener generations allocated under a token, timers whose fires are held until acked and never written to the control stream, and a due index. Every client action is one store step. Invariants with one reversed witness each (StaleReportRefused, IncarnationNeverReused, LinkNamesTheCurrentGeneration, ProofNeverPastHardDeadline, GenerationAllocatedOnce, InstallIsIdempotentByToken, FireHeldUntilAcked, OneFirePerSettle, TimerIdIsStable, EarlierTimerEndsWait, CommsNeverWritesTheBus, CapabilityCurrentOrNone, CrashWritesNothing) and liveness under written assumptions (EventuallyDelivered, ProofLapsesWhenListenerGone). Eighteen TLC cases, each under the runner's cap. Absorbs the hook model draft tla-hook-delivers-rearms-and-sees-partners and the presence-batch-turn model draft, which retire with batch turns. Its tests are comms-test-plan. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: tla/RUNS.tsv holds a current record, as declared, for all eighteen comms cases and tlacheck groups --stale prints [] on a bench.

Target: v1.3

From: the coordinator's draft card of 2026-10-12, from the owner's direction

### The comms module holds presence, capability and timers

pkg/comms: the store side as Lua functions in Redis (connect, report, capability, arm and disarm, install, settle, detect, status; keys under comms:) loaded through pkg/redisfn, and a thin Go client of tla/Comms.tla, each operation one FCALL and Wait one blocking read, so every business operation is one round trip. nova-bus stays the one mail path: comms holds only references to bus ids, never writes a bus key and never acks. The incarnation is a fresh random value every later call carries; a stale report, an orphan settle and a past deadline are refused by name. docs/SPEC-COMMS.md is the one spec: the key layout, the two deadlines, the token rule, the fires held until acked, the collision assumption, the liveness assumptions, the durability envelope and the one-round-trip boundary. The loopback-or-tailnet address rule (local-only-address-check, nova-sprint roadmap) is one function here. The module is for every tool that needs it, never part of nova-bus, and never imports the friend daemon. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: TestEveryCommsOperationIsOneRoundTrip shows one round trip per function and per Wait on a real Redis, and no go-redis call sits inside a loop in pkg/comms.

Target: v1.3

From: the coordinator's draft card of 2026-10-12, from the owner's direction: one shared comms module, Redis as the server

### nova-hook connects a client to the server

nova-hook is a client's connection to the server and nothing else: connect, prove who it is (the hook record, the challenge, prove, unhook and status stay as they are), arm the push listener through pkg/comms with the generation allocated in the store under a token, deliver pushes into the session (one HOOK PUSH line per message per process, the drain cursor the oldest pending bus entry so nothing in the gap between generations is lost), keep the connection alive (a one-round-trip heartbeat and the one recurring re-arm timer, consumed by the live session, which runs the hook again), and say when it is not connected (unread, read, superseded, store-lost). A store timer never re-arms an in-session listener and the hook never reconnects on its own: after a store loss only a live turn arms again. docs/SPEC-HOOK.md gains the session bridge, one measured recipe per harness, with none, measured for a harness without one. Replay after a reconnect delivers only the unacked pushes; a reader that is not the seat hooks like any client. Every bus and friend verb refuses until hooked (the v1.2.18 and v1.2.17 rows of the fixes ledgers are this entry's point-release half). Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: a bus message sent before Arm and one sent during the loop each print one HOOK PUSH line, a re-arm fires once per period with no catch-up, and the heartbeat is one round trip, all on a real Redis.

Target: v1.3

From: the coordinator's draft card of 2026-10-12, from the owner's direction: a client connects to the server

### nova-wake records what each harness can do, and that Codex has no wake

A thin tool on pkg/comms with three verbs, each one round trip: record writes the capability record (link and wake, with the method, build, host, session kind and measured-at as evidence) from the tool's own harness table, only for the installation the row was measured on, and refuses a harness not in the table; check runs one paged detect of the due index; status shows presence, the capability and the armed link in separate columns, never a word meaning alive. The one row this round is Codex: link pushed-in-turn, wake none, because no harness offers a measured atomic start-if-idle; no executor is built, and the two Codex wake drafts wait until one does. The table of which harnesses a process can wake (spec-work-harness-wake-table) is this record. The tracer bullet that proves the comms path end to end on one named installation is written into docs/SPEC-COMMS.md as the acceptance the coordinator runs after this lands. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): SPEC-WORK records which harnesses a process can wake (spec-work-harness-wake-table). Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: nova-wake status on a test store shows capability and the armed link in separate columns, the Codex record wake none with its evidence, and every verb is one round trip.

Target: v1.3

From: the coordinator's draft card of 2026-10-12, from the owner's ask to wake an idle friend without queuing or steering

### nova-bus2 output lines state the reason, counts and digests a caller needs

The ack, send and recv lines of nova-bus2 carry the facts a caller needs: why an ack was false, the byte count and digest of a send, that an empty wait is a result and not a failure, and how many messages wait behind the oldest one. Text, JSON and help all say the same thing. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: every ack, send and recv line of nova-bus carries its reason, counts and digests, pinned by a transcript test per line.

Target: v1.3

Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: a bus client against an unreachable address returns within its deadline in a test, and no bus wait is unbounded.

### TLA+ models for friend lanes, delivery, presence and session checks

Model the friend daemon's one-shot lanes, message delivery and acks, presence across batch turns, the session check file and the lane governor, and check them with TLC. Re-aimed at the lane protocol: the model is of a thin client that asks the server what it holds at its epoch, runs, reports by the server's ids and asks again, with no lane table, cached epoch or local recovery; the delivery, presence and session-check halves retire with the comms module. Its tests are lanes-test-plan. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: the lane protocol model and its reversed witnesses have current TLC records in tla/RUNS.tsv and every lane action in the code cites the model.

Target: v1.3

From: card from the sprint store (2026-10-10); card moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-04)

### One-shot workers per card, friends included

Every card gets a fresh worker session that ends when the card ends. No worker sits idle between cards holding a session, and no session carries one card's context into the next. Long-lived sessions are kept only for coordination: the seat and the friends' chat. This changes the friend default from batch to one-shot, makes a lane one session, and changes the friend daemon's lifecycle to match. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): One-shot friend lanes replace the hand-written runner scripts (friend-one-shot-lanes-replace-runner-scripts). Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: every friend and member runs one session per card by default, the batch delivery mode is gone from the config, and a 140-width run on the bench shows one process per working card.

Already in the code: nova-swarm runs one task per launch (cmd/nova-swarm/main.go:1). Friends have a one-shot mode (internal/friend/lanes.go:26), but the default is batch (internal/config/kind.go:213-215). The gap is one-shot as the default for every friend, and batch delivery retired for work.

Why it waits: A change of the default delivery model, not a fix.

Target: v1.3

Done when: one lane engine per one-shot friend holds its row at width through an adopt on the bench, measured by the friend's row equalling its live lanes for an hour.

### Extract the roadmap tool into nova-roadmap

The roadmap and fixes code exists twice: here as internal/roadmap, internal/roadmap/sexp and tools/roadmap, and in nova-sprint as internal/roadmap, internal/roadmapdoc, tools/roadmap and the nova-work roadmap verbs, with two diverging copies of the generator. Unify the s-expression format first; then one module and one CLI, nova-roadmap, living in nova-sprint: it reads and writes the data, renders ROADMAP.md and FIXES.md, and runs the sync check. ## v1.3 I. Routes, rate limits and spend

The global per-model budget, provider error handling, tier measurement and spend reconciliation. Build order.

### Routes, rate limits and spend: test plan

The routes theme's tests, written from docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md before the theme's first implementation entry, which cites this one: unit tests of the token bucket with a fake clock; functional tests on a real Redis, one per Lua function of the budget; an integration run of callers on three bench machines sharing one budget; the stress drag (10 requests a second per model across the fleet, never exceeded in any one-second window); the budget model with its reversed witnesses, checked by TLC on a bench; and its rows in the parallel release checks, under two minutes. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: each tier above has a named test for the routes theme, listed in docs/TEST-PLAN-v1.3.md, red before the theme's code and green after, with the 10 requests a second per model across the fleet recorded.

Target: v1.3

From: the owner, 2026-10-12

### A model has a requests-per-second budget, global across the fleet

A budget per model (and per key), in requests per second and per minute, kept in nova-config beside the model and enforced where the request is made: the harness adapter's lane start and the router. The budget is global across every machine: one bucket per model and key in the sprint store's Redis, taken atomically by a Lua function that refills by the server clock and hands out one token or the wait, never a counter per process or per machine. A caller that cannot take a token waits the returned time and never calls the provider without one; a refused-by-budget lane waits and is never a failure. The dashboard shows the budget and the use, and a 429 from the provider lowers the budget mechanically and is reported as what it is. A pure token-bucket module with a fake clock; a TLA+ model of N callers on M machines sharing one bucket (NeverOverBudget over any one-second window, EveryWaiterStarts, and a reversed witness with a per-machine bucket that exceeds the budget). This is the global per-model rate limit the Mercury 3 heavy route and the tier measurements wait on; the per-route per-minute budget it replaces was the weaker form. Absorbs (de-duplicated 2026-10-12): A route carries a request budget and a jittered rest end (route-rate-budget-and-jitter, nova-sprint roadmap); Per-provider and per-model concurrency ceilings with error watch and spill (provider-capacity-ceilings-and-spill, nova-sprint roadmap). Its tests are routes-test-plan. Lands only after the v1.3 test plan (v1-3-test-plan). Done when: 140 callers on three bench machines sharing one model budget of 10 a second never exceed 10 in any one-second window, no caller starves, and the TLC run of NeverOverBudget and EveryWaiterStarts is recorded.

Why it waits: The owner, 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09: per-model pacing, global across all fleet machines; v1.3, not v1.2 reliability.

Target: v1.3

## Lessons from Prime Agent's rewrite

Prime Intellect's write-up of rewriting Prime Agent with AI workers (https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/prime-agent-rust) names what made a large AI-built rewrite hold together. Each item is one of those lessons, checked against nova's code at dev 9ff68178: what already exists is named by file and line, and the item covers the rest.

### A differential parity harness for rewrites

When a tool is rewritten, the old and the new run the same inputs side by side and their outputs are diffed against goldens: terminal frames, transcripts, model requests and protocol messages. Beside the diffs, a feature ledger marks each feature of the old tool as matching, partial or missing in the new one, and the rewrite ships when no row is missing that the owner has not waived. First use: nova-local to barrio. The v1.3 rename of nova-swarm to nova-worker is a rename, not a rewrite; its guard is the one-release shim and the existing tests.

Why it waits: New test machinery, and its first user, barrio, is itself after v1.4.

Target: later

### A performance hillclimb loop

Performance work runs as a loop. Profile, and write each idea down as a hypothesis in a backlog. Run the current build and the candidate interleaved on the same bench, many rounds, so noise falls on both alike. Keep a change only when it wins the interleaved runs and two reviewers agree it does not change behavior. There are no numeric targets: the loop keeps the wins it can show. Candidates: the sprint tick, the dashboard's one-second update, and the lander's gate wall.

Why it waits: Performance work is neither a fix nor v1.4 cleanup.

Target: later

### Pin the upstream provider per route and log it in usage rows

Routes through an aggregator pin the provider order and forbid fallbacks, so the same model does not cost many times more through another door. The chosen provider is logged per usage row so cost can be traced.

Every job clones the repository for itself, which repeats the same work. Share a cached clone or a reference clone across jobs.

From: issue #80

Card cost is context times harness turns, because every tool call resends the context. A card whose steps are named runs as a pipeline of stateless calls with the harness running the tools, and reads cap their reasoning.

Target: later

From: issue #855; issue #856

## Friends

New ways for friends to connect and work.

### New friend routes and verbs

Codex and Claude Code routes into an open chat; nova-friend verbs for peers, screen, watch and renew; presence kept off the sprint server; a bus store that does not need the sprint; and the friend daemons adopted by the fleet. Presence is the comms module's (the-comms-module-holds-presence-capability-and-timers); only the verbs remain here.

Why it waits: New capability.

Target: later

Replaces 9 open sprint cards, each mapped to `friend-routes-and-verbs`.

### Mark bus messages by sender authority in a friend's session

A friend delivers a bus message as an instruction only when it comes from the coordinator seat holder. Every other message, and every message while the seat is unknown, is delivered as data.

Target: later

From: card moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-04)

### Per-card token cap and cheaper deliveries for per-token friends

Every one-shot friend lane counts tokens and stops at a per-card cap. Briefs cite rules by reference and each prompt starts with one stable prefix to cut tokens per landed card.

Target: later

From: cards moved out of the sprint (work record, 2026-10-04); card from the sprint store (2026-10-10)

Two sessions of one participant share a single cursor, so the second has no usable inbox advance or wait. A per session cursor fixes this.

Target: later

The dispatcher picks a model from the worker and profile files and never asks the ladder. A card the ladder marks for a child or the bus must not run on a mechanical model.

Target: later

From: issue #1486

### Token, call, cost and in-flight limits per card and per route

The native path enforces token, call and cost caps and an idle watch, budgets follow each route's cost and caching, and requests in flight are capped per route. The per-model budget is a-model-has-a-requests-per-second-budget (v1.3); the idle watch remains here.

Target: later

From: issue #1545; issue #1811; issue #2580; issue #5094; issue #917

The swarm result records per-request send, first-byte and done times so a wall ending says who stalled.

Each card runs a full harness process of several hundred megabytes, which sets every machine's width. Options to measure are a shared server per machine, heap limits and compressed swap.

## Far

Directions, not plans. Nothing in v1.x builds toward these yet.

### Thousands of self-organizing workers

A system in which thousands of workers organize themselves: they find work, split it, and check each other, with no central dealer. The v1.3 rename retires the nova-swarm name, so no tool holds the word swarm when this is designed.

Why it waits: A direction, not a plan.

Target: later

One batch applies across 2 to 16 tables, and receipt pages refuse missing history. Creates over 256 cells are refused before scoring.

Target: later
